purpose: Map workload traits to recommended Firebase product boundaries.

decision_nodes.why: Firestore fits query-driven document access when denormalization is acceptable.
Choose only when the workload is naturally tree-shaped or sync-oriented and does not benefit from Firestore's query model.
Object storage is the correct boundary for files, media, and blobs instead of Firestore documents.
Privileged operations, external API calls, and mediated workflows belong in backend code.
Hosting fits frontend delivery and framework integration paths.
App Check helps reduce abuse from illegitimate app clients.
Relational workloads should not be forced into Firestore-only design.

operator_prompts: What are the exact read and write paths?
Which operations must be allowed directly from the client?
Which operations require trusted backend mediation?
Will this workload need joins, reporting, or SQL-style transactions?
What is the expected read volume per screen, per listener, and per session?
